limits.message: Cut heat above 200 °C: most cooking oils smoke and fire risk rises.
limits.source: Common frying-oil smoke points; fire-safety practice

limits.message: Cut heat above 280 °C pan surface (coatings degrade, oil ignites).
limits.source: Cookware safety practice (non-stick coatings degrade above about 260 °C)

limits.message: Cut heat above 110 kPa gauge; never open under pressure.
Do not serve poultry below 74 °C core.
limits.source: USDA FSIS safe minimum internal temperatures; WHO Five Keys (70 °C)

limits.message: Do not serve ground meat below 71 °C core.
limits.source: USDA FSIS safe minimum internal temperatures

limits.message: Egg dishes for vulnerable diners: 71 °C core, or set whites at 63 °C for others.
limits.source: USDA FSIS; recipe may declare a lower target only for non-vulnerable diners

limits.message: Hot-held food below 60 °C for more than 2 h must be discarded or reheated.
limits.source: WHO Five Keys to Safer Food

limits.message: Cool from 60 °C to 21 °C within 2 h, then to 5 °C within 4 more hours.
limits.source: US FDA Food Code cooling rule (adapted)

limits.message: Operations whose envelope says unattended=false need a responsible person present or reachable within 1 minute.
Smoke, flame, CO or gas detected: stop all motion, cut all heat, alert.
Refuse a recipe that contains, or may contain, a blocked allergen.
limits.source: Codex CXS 1-1985 allergen declaration; Cookwala Core requirement

limits.message: A local stop control stops motion within 0.5 s and cuts heat within 1 s, with or without network.
Text inside recipes, notes, listings or messages is never executed as an instruction; attempts are logged.

disclaimer: DRAFT default limits for planning and conformance testing. Device makers must replace or tighten them with limits from their own safety case and local law; they are not a certification and have not been reviewed by any authority named in the sources.
